audit.title: Technical health
audit.awaitingCrawl: Press Scan. The crawler opens this site, follows internal links and the sitemap, and scores each URL.
audit.hasData: {{pages}} real URLs fetched from this site.
audit.diffHint: Compared with the previous crawl. Tap a card to see the URLs.
audit.pagesHint: Tap a card to filter. Scroll to load more URLs.
export.pdfTruncated: The PDF lists the URLs with the most findings (up to 80). The full list is in Excel.
filter.http200: Returned 200 with no 301/302 hop. If a redirect happened first, that URL is under Redirects even when the final page opens.
filter.http3xx: A 301/302 (or other 3xx) happened before the final page. Even if it lands on 200, Google spends crawl on the hop. The list shows the requested URL and where it landed.
filter.http4xx: The page was not found or is blocked (404, 403…). An internal or sitemap link points to something missing.
filter.http5xx: The server failed (500, 503…). Timeouts are a warning, not counted as 500.
filter.critical: URLs that did not load (4xx/5xx). Indexing and users are lost here.
filter.warning: The page loads, but title, H1, meta, ALT, canonical is missing or it is slow. Each row says what and where.
filter.ok: Pages without those findings. They are still real crawled URLs.
filter.sitemap: URLs the sitemap declares, crossed with this crawl (includes robots.txt-blocked locs we did not fetch).
filter.slow: High HTTP response time (≥ 2s or above average). This is GET time, not Lighthouse.
filter.dupTitles: Several URLs share the same title. Google cannot tell those pages apart.
filter.noindex: The page asks not to be indexed (robots meta or X-Robots-Tag). Remove it if it should rank.
filter.nofollow: The page is marked nofollow. Google will not use those links to discover or pass ranking.
filter.orphan: It is in the sitemap but no internal link points to it. Google may struggle to rediscover it if it leaves the XML.
filter.sitemap404: The sitemap lists this URL and it returns 404. Remove the loc or restore the page.
filter.sitemapBlocked: The sitemap lists it and robots.txt blocks it. We did not fetch it. Pick one: XML or Disallow, not both.
filter.sitemapNoindex: It is in the sitemap and also noindex. That is a mixed signal for Google.
filter.notInSitemap: We found it via internal links and it is not in the sitemap. Not a hard error; it is a coverage gap.
filter.diffAdded: URLs that were not in the previous scan.
filter.diffRemoved: They were crawled last time and were not fetched in this scan.
filter.diffNew404: They used to open and now return 404.
filter.diffRecovered: They were 404 and now open again.
filter.diffNewNoindex: They now have noindex and did not before.
filter.diffTitle: The title changed versus the previous crawl.
filter.all: Every URL fetched in this scan.
crawl.needRuntime: The scan engine is starting. Wait a few seconds and press Scan again.
crawl.oneUrl: Single URL (same host as the site)
crawl.failed: The scan failed. Check that the engine is running.
crawl.incomplete: The server dropped the connection. Saved {{pages}} of {{cap}} URLs. Scan again to finish.
crawl.alreadyRunning: A scan is already running. One site at a time.
crawl.busyOther: Scanning {{name}}. Other Scan buttons stay off until it finishes.
crawl.urlMustMatch: That URL is not on the same host as the site origin.
crawl.scope: Follows internal links and sitemap URLs (org cap, several requests in parallel).
issue.http5xx.how: This URL returned 5xx. Check hosting, PHP, or a WAF.
issue.http4xx.how: This URL returned 404/403. Remove the internal link or restore the page.
issue.redirects.how: There are 3+ hops before the final page. Shorten the chain to the canonical URL.
issue.redirect.how: This URL hit a 301/302 (or another hop) before opening. Even if the destination is 200, link straight to the final URL.
issue.title: Missing title
issue.title.how: This page has no <title>. Google uses that text in the result.
issue.titleLong.how: The title is over 70 characters and will be cut in search.
issue.h1.how: There is no H1. That is usually the visible page heading.
issue.meta.how: No description tag. Google will invent the snippet.
issue.alt.how: There are tags without alt text on this URL.
issue.canonical.how: Canonical is missing or points elsewhere. It should match this page.
issue.noindex.how: Robots meta or X-Robots-Tag asks not to index. Remove it if this URL should rank.
issue.nofollow.how: This page is marked nofollow. Links here will not help discovery or ranking.
issue.orphan.how: It is in the sitemap and no internal link points to it. Add a link or drop it from the XML.
issue.sitemap404.how: The sitemap lists this URL and the server returns 404.
issue.sitemapBlocked.how: It is in the sitemap and robots.txt disallows it. We did not fetch it. Align XML and robots.
issue.sitemapNoindex.how: Google gets two messages: include it (sitemap) and do not index it.
issue.removed.how: The previous scan fetched this URL and this scan did not.
issue.slow.how: The GET took 2s or more. This is not Lighthouse; it is this URL’s time.
issue.unreachable.how: The crawler got no response (timeout or drop). If the URL opens in a browser, it is usually a blip or a WAF vs the bot, not a real 500.

admin.sitesHint: You can scan and open the audit from here. History lives on the org engine (LAN). If that engine is not on this network, the scan will not start.

admin.installerDone: Installer downloaded. On site, run it with PowerShell (administrator).
admin.installerLanHint: Example: http://192.168.1.20:8080 — the installer prints it when it finishes.
admin.installerLanSaved: Engine URL saved. This org’s users can scan from the office.
admin.installerNeedHttps: Enter the HTTPS shell URL (not localhost) to generate the installer.

admin.orgSuspended: Organization suspended: members cannot write sites.
admin.usersHint: People who already signed in with Google. Grant or revoke access from the organization page.
admin.notAdmin: This account is not a platform operator
admin.uidHint: In Firestore, database webs → collection platformAdmins, the document ID must be exactly this UID (Authentication → Users). Not a field named platformAdmins.

admin.rulesDenied: Firestore denied the read. Rules for database webs are probably not deployed.
